key_insight: Task transformation can turn open-ended LLM improvement into a verifiable reward problem by designing proxy environments with self-generated supervision.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable training path for improving LLMs on non-verifiable tasks without relying on costly or biased human/judge-based rewards.
method: Reframe open-ended tasks as verifiable proxy tasks using internal rules and interaction outcomes.
Instantiate the framework with SpyRL, a multi-agent self-play setting inspired by Who Is the Spy?
Use predetermined spy identity and voting outcomes to produce fully verifiable rewards.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on text summarization, creative writing, and mathematical reasoning, where SpyRL outperforms existing self-improvement methods on non-verifiable tasks and improves verifiable reasoning tasks.
watch_item: Performance depends on how well the proxy task preserves the target task’s semantics; poorly designed transformations could optimize the wrong behavior.
paper_title: From RLVR to RLSVR: Task Transformation Induces Self-Verifiable Rewards for Open-Ended LLM Self-Improvement
